blb.name: Bad Luck Brian
blb.meaning: An ordinary attempt produces a sharply disproportionate unlucky result.
blb.writing_guide: Put the reasonable action first and the unlucky consequence second. Apply the role to a project, process, or yourself, never an employee or customer.
anti_patterns: Do not target a real person or vulnerable group.
Do not use an expected result; the failure must feel absurdly unlucky.

slots.role: Top caption names the normal attempt.
Bottom caption gives the disproportionate failure.

invariants: The second line must be worse than the first line reasonably predicts.
The joke target must be a system, project, or self-own.

assessment.origin: Advice-animal macro built around Kyle Craven's school portrait and a run of catastrophically unlucky outcomes.
assessment.safety: The template historically humiliates a named-looking person. Hold until the selector can enforce project or self-directed targets.
assessment.legibility: PASS: every caption and image role remains readable in the exact 360px contact-sheet tile.
assessment.admission_rationale: The failure relationship is useful, but its default human target conflicts with the operator-not-fool rule.

box.name: What's in the box!?
box.meaning: A promised container or package conceals an alarming unknown.
box.writing_guide: Name the supposedly complete package, then use the fixed question to expose missing visibility.
anti_patterns: Do not use for ordinary curiosity.
Do not invoke harm, victims, or the film's violent reveal.

slots.role: Top caption names the package whose contents are unclear.
Bottom caption is the fixed demand to see inside.

invariants: The first line must name something presented as complete while its actual contents remain unknown.

assessment.origin: Reaction from the climax of the film Se7en, whose concealed box contains evidence of a murder.
assessment.safety: The recognizable meaning depends on a violent murder reveal.
assessment.legibility: PASS: every caption and image role remains readable in the exact 360px contact-sheet tile.
assessment.admission_rationale: The violence is not incidental to the template's suspense, so it fails the injury and disaster gate.

cake.name: Office Space Milton
cake.meaning: A promised benefit or resource quietly fails to appear.
cake.writing_guide: Set the occasion on top and adapt the fixed complaint below. The missing item should have been explicitly promised, not merely hoped for.
anti_patterns: Do not use for a vague disappointment.
Do not make an employee's exclusion the joke.

slots.role: Top caption names the event or promise.
Bottom caption begins with the fixed complaint.

invariants: The missing item must be something the setup explicitly led the subject to expect.
operator_example: I was told there would be data access

assessment.origin: Milton's repeated cake complaint in the 1999 workplace comedy Office Space.
assessment.safety: Fictional workplace character. Keep the target on a missing organizational promise, not employee exclusion.
assessment.legibility: PASS: every caption and image role remains readable in the exact 360px contact-sheet tile.
assessment.admission_rationale: Adds broken organizational promises in a workplace-native format.

disastergirl.name: Disaster Girl
disastergirl.meaning: A calm observer appears to have caused the destruction behind them.
disastergirl.writing_guide: Name the plan or result, then imply smug responsibility.
anti_patterns: Do not use real disasters.
Do not imply a named person caused harm.

slots.role: Top caption names the destructive result.
Bottom caption implies it was planned.

invariants: The background destruction is the reason the calm expression reads as culpable.

assessment.origin: A 2005 photograph of a child watching firefighters conduct a controlled burn, later edited into disaster scenes.
assessment.safety: The joke depends on fire and implied responsibility for destruction.
assessment.legibility: PASS: every caption and image role remains readable in the exact 360px contact-sheet tile.
assessment.admission_rationale: Directly conflicts with the catalog's disaster gate.

dragon.name: What Color Do You Want Your Dragon
dragon.meaning: A supposedly ordinary request is treated as less realistic than receiving a dragon.
dragon.writing_guide: Use the one editable line for the initial request. It should sound reasonable to the requester but impossible under the stated constraints.
anti_patterns: Do not ask for a genuinely trivial thing.
Do not require the reader to know missing dialogue outside the template.

slots.role: The editable speech bubble contains the request rejected as unrealistic.

invariants: The fixed dragon offer must be easier than granting the editable request.
operator_example: A reliable model with no evaluation budget

assessment.origin: An illustrated Tumblr exchange in which a request for a boyfriend is judged less realistic than a dragon.
assessment.safety: Illustrated fictional exchange. Avoid stereotypes about relationships or protected traits.
assessment.legibility: FAIL: the editable speech bubble remains too small at the audited 360px width, even with a short example.
assessment.admission_rationale: The impossible-constraints relationship is useful, but the editable bubble is too small at the audited 360px width.

elf.name: You Sit on a Throne of Lies
elf.meaning: A confident assurance is dismissed as obviously false.
elf.writing_guide: Put the assurance on top and preserve the fixed accusation below. Use only when the post has evidence that contradicts the assurance.
anti_patterns: Do not accuse a named company or person of lying without strong evidence.
Do not use for uncertainty or a mere prediction miss.

slots.role: Top caption states the contradicted assurance.
Bottom caption preserves the established rebuke.
slots.required_regex: (?i)^you sit on a throne of lies[.!]*$

invariants: The post must contain evidence that makes the assurance false, not debatable.
operator_example: The vendor says setup takes one day
You sit on a throne of lies

assessment.origin: Buddy confronts a department-store Santa in the 2003 film Elf; the phrase became a reaction to false statements.
assessment.safety: Fictional confrontation. Restrict accusations to substantiated claims or generic/self-directed examples.
assessment.legibility: PASS: every caption and image role remains readable in the exact 360px contact-sheet tile.
assessment.admission_rationale: Adds blunt evidence-backed contradiction, stronger than Agnes's knowing wink.

friends.name: Are You Two Friends?
friends.meaning: Two parties give incompatible answers about whether they are aligned.
friends.writing_guide: Label the outside observer first, then the party that says yes and the party that says no. Use a real asymmetry in incentives or expectations.
anti_patterns: Do not use for two parties who simply disagree on a topic.
Do not swap the yes and no roles after rendering.

slots.role: First overlay labels the person asking about the relationship.
Second overlay labels the left character, who answers no.
Third overlay labels the right character, who answers yes.

invariants: One labeled party must plausibly answer yes and the other no to the same relationship question.

assessment.origin: A Star Trek: Voyager exchange in which Tuvok says he and Paris are friends while Paris says they are not.
assessment.safety: Fictional dialogue. Use organizational roles, not protected groups or political caricatures.
assessment.legibility: PASS: every caption and image role remains readable in the exact 360px contact-sheet tile.
assessment.admission_rationale: Adds asymmetric alignment, a common source of failed internal AI programs.

headaches.name: Types of Headaches
headaches.meaning: One process or condition causes pain far beyond the ordinary categories shown beside it.
headaches.writing_guide: Use the editable final label for a specific operational nuisance whose repeated burden is the joke.
anti_patterns: Do not joke about a person's illness.
Do not use a broad topic such as 'AI' without naming the actual burden.

slots.role: The editable fourth label names the outsized operational pain.

invariants: The custom condition must be plausibly more frustrating than the three fixed headache categories in the image.

assessment.origin: A headache-location infographic turned into a four-panel comparison with a fully red final head.
assessment.safety: Medical imagery, but no victim or injury. Keep the comparison figurative and work-related.
assessment.legibility: PASS: every caption and image role remains readable in the exact 360px contact-sheet tile.
assessment.admission_rationale: Adds a compact way to show cumulative operational pain.

interesting.name: The Most Interesting Man in the World
interesting.meaning: A rare behavior is paired with the speaker's reliably distinctive way of doing it.
interesting.writing_guide: Preserve the 'I don't always' and 'but when I do' syntax. The second line should expose a specific habit, contradiction, or preference.
anti_patterns: Do not use as generic self-praise.
Do not drop the fixed two-part syntax.

slots.role: Top caption begins the fixed rarity setup.
Bottom caption completes the fixed exception.

invariants: The second line must describe what reliably happens on the rare occasions named in line one.
operator_example: I don't always automate a process
But when I do, I keep the exception queue

assessment.origin: Advice-animal macro based on Jonathan Goldsmith's Dos Equis advertisement and its 'I don't always ... but when I do' line.
assessment.safety: Commercial character and actor likeness. Avoid implying endorsement or copying beer branding into the caption.
assessment.legibility: PASS: every caption and image role remains readable in the exact 360px contact-sheet tile.
assessment.admission_rationale: Adds a strong fixed syntax for revealing an uncommon but consistent operating habit.

ive.name: Jony Ive Redesigns Things
ive.meaning: A polished redesign removes or obscures something people actually need.
ive.writing_guide: Name the removed function first, then use a polished assurance below. The joke is misplaced design confidence, not appearance alone.
anti_patterns: Do not attack Jony Ive personally.
Do not use for an ordinary visual redesign with no lost function.

slots.role: Top caption names what the redesign removed.
Bottom caption gives the confident product-language reassurance.

invariants: The redesign must make the underlying task harder while presenting itself as an improvement.

assessment.origin: Memegen attributes the image to Apple's former design chief, but its source points to an Apple biography rather than a cultural-history page.
assessment.safety: Real identifiable executive. The current evidence does not establish the template's mutation or accepted caption structure.
assessment.legibility: PASS: every caption and image role remains readable in the exact 360px contact-sheet tile.
assessment.admission_rationale: Hold until a cultural source and three documented uses verify the redesign relationship.

jw.name: Probably Not a Good Idea
jw.meaning: A concrete reckless action receives an understated warning after it is proposed or revealed.
jw.writing_guide: State the questionable action as a direct question, then preserve the calm verdict. Use a specific operational decision, not general AI anxiety.
anti_patterns: Do not turn the warning into fear bait.
Do not use when the downside is merely uncertain.

slots.role: Top caption asks whether the risky action really happened.
Bottom caption is the understated fixed judgment.

invariants: The post must explain the foreseeable downside of the specific action.
operator_example: You gave the agent production write access?

assessment.origin: Chris Pratt's Jurassic World character reacts to the creation of a new dinosaur in the film's 2014 trailer.
assessment.safety: Fictional film character. Avoid using it for vague catastrophe predictions.
assessment.legibility: PASS: every caption and image role remains readable in the exact 360px contact-sheet tile.
assessment.admission_rationale: Adds dry understatement after a concrete risky decision.

khaby-lame.name: Khaby Lame Shrug
khaby-lame.meaning: An elaborate workaround loses to an obvious, simpler method.
khaby-lame.writing_guide: Put the overengineered method first and the direct alternative second. Both must solve the same problem.
anti_patterns: Do not use for two mere preferences.
Do not imply that a complex task is easy when the post shows otherwise.

slots.role: Top-left caption names the unnecessary workaround.
Bottom-left caption names the direct alternative indicated by the shrug.

invariants: Both lines must pursue the same outcome, and the second must remove needless steps.
operator_example: Build a chatbot for every policy

assessment.origin: Khaby Lame's 2021 reaction to a contrived pizza life hack, followed by a shrug toward the obvious method.
assessment.safety: Real creator likeness. Keep the contrast on methods and never on identity or ability.
assessment.legibility: PASS: every caption and image role remains readable in the exact 360px contact-sheet tile.
assessment.admission_rationale: Adds a familiar overengineering-versus-direct-fix relationship.

kramer.name: Kramer, What's Going On In There?
kramer.meaning: A visible symptom prompts a question and receives an unexpectedly specific explanation.
kramer.writing_guide: Keep the first line as a question about the odd visible result. The second line names the surprising mechanism in plain language.
anti_patterns: Do not use a generic 'AI is weird' explanation.
Do not make the answer longer than the image can carry.

slots.role: Top dialogue asks what is causing the visible anomaly.
Bottom dialogue gives the specific, surprising cause.

invariants: The second line must actually explain the first line's visible anomaly.
operator_example: Why is the queue turning red?
The agent approved its own exceptions

assessment.origin: A Seinfeld apartment scene whose red light is repeatedly relabeled with strange fictional causes.
assessment.safety: Fictional sitcom scene. Keep explanations about systems, not groups or people.
assessment.legibility: PASS: every caption and image role remains readable in the exact 360px contact-sheet tile.
assessment.admission_rationale: Adds symptom-to-unexpected-cause storytelling.

light.name: Everything the Light Touches is Our Kingdom
light.meaning: A proud claim of broad scope is immediately bounded by one conspicuous excluded area.
light.writing_guide: Ask about the excluded area first and answer with the boundary second. Use a real ownership, access, or support boundary.
anti_patterns: Do not use for an arbitrary disliked thing.
Do not hide the boundary that makes the post's claim accurate.

slots.role: First dialogue asks about the conspicuous excluded area.
Second dialogue states that the area is outside the claimed scope.

invariants: The excluded area must materially limit the broad scope implied by the image.
operator_example: That's beyond the pilot. You must never go there.

assessment.origin: The Lion King scene defining the kingdom and warning Simba away from the shadowy place became a scope and gatekeeping macro.
assessment.safety: Animated fictional characters. Avoid political or protected-group gatekeeping.
assessment.legibility: PASS: every caption and image role remains readable in the exact 360px contact-sheet tile.
assessment.admission_rationale: Adds explicit scope boundaries, a recurring truth in AI pilots.

nails.name: Guy Hammering Nails Into Sand
nails.meaning: A tool or representation tries futilely to impose stable boundaries on something that will not hold them.
nails.writing_guide: Label the actor, the method, and the unstable medium. The method should be structurally incapable of controlling the medium.
anti_patterns: Do not use for generic hard work.
Do not claim futility when the method merely needs improvement.

slots.role: First label names who is trying to impose order.
Second label names the rigid tool or representation.
Third label names what cannot hold the imposed boundary.

invariants: The method must fail because the target cannot retain the imposed structure.
operator_example: An agent that changes tools mid-run

assessment.origin: A photograph cataloged by Memegen, Imgflip, and OldMeme; no reliable cultural-origin account was found.
assessment.safety: No obvious harmful subject, but the source and established caption relationship remain weakly documented.
assessment.legibility: PASS: every caption and image role remains readable in the exact 360px contact-sheet tile.
assessment.admission_rationale: Hold until a cultural source establishes familiarity and the three-label relation beyond isolated catalog examples.

philosoraptor.name: Philosoraptor
philosoraptor.meaning: A familiar premise leads to a playful paradox or semantic question.
philosoraptor.writing_guide: State the premise first and make the second line a genuine twist created by the premise. Prefer wordplay over fake profundity.
anti_patterns: Do not use as a generic question card.
Do not present a factual claim as a paradox without checking it.

slots.role: Top caption states the familiar premise.
Bottom caption asks the playful consequence.

invariants: The question must follow from the wording or logic of the premise, not merely share a topic.
operator_example: If the AI learned from our old process
Is automation just faster institutional memory?

assessment.origin: Advice-animal illustration of a contemplative velociraptor used for absurd philosophical questions and paradoxes.
assessment.safety: Illustrated animal. Avoid laundering misinformation as a clever question.
assessment.legibility: PASS: every caption and image role remains readable in the exact 360px contact-sheet tile.
assessment.admission_rationale: Adds genuine premise-to-paradox wordplay.

spirit.name: Fake Spirit Halloween Costume
spirit.meaning: A recognizable organizational type is packaged as a costume with a revealing inventory of traits.
spirit.writing_guide: Name the role, preserve 'Includes:', and list three concrete artifacts or habits. The list should reveal the type without insults.
anti_patterns: Do not target a protected class or individual employee.
Do not use three synonyms as the included items.

slots.role: First line names the organizational type on the package.
Second line preserves the package label.
Third line is the first concrete included trait.
Fourth line is the second concrete included trait.
Fifth line is the third concrete included trait.

invariants: The three included items must be distinct, concrete evidence of the named type.

assessment.origin: Edits of Spirit Halloween costume packaging became a format for labeling a character type and listing its recognizable contents.
assessment.safety: Corporate parody is acceptable. Avoid protected groups, appearance, or demeaning employee stereotypes.
assessment.legibility: PASS: every caption and image role remains readable in the exact 360px contact-sheet tile.
assessment.admission_rationale: Adds an inventory joke that can expose the ingredients of a familiar failure pattern.

spongebob.name: Mocking Spongebob
spongebob.meaning: A statement is repeated in alternating case to belittle the speaker.
spongebob.writing_guide: Repeat the claim in mocking typography.
anti_patterns: Do not ridicule a person or group.
Do not substitute mockery for a factual rebuttal.

slots.role: Top caption quotes the statement.
Bottom caption repeats it in alternating case.

invariants: The second line must mock the first line rather than add an argument.

assessment.origin: A SpongeBob reaction image used specifically to mimic and ridicule another person's statement.
assessment.safety: Its established mechanism is humiliation rather than clarification.
assessment.legibility: PASS: every caption and image role remains readable in the exact 360px contact-sheet tile.
assessment.admission_rationale: Conflicts with the operator-not-fool rule and rewards unsupported sneering.

stop.name: Stop It Patrick You're Scaring Him
stop.meaning: A misunderstood label escalates through six dialogue turns until the subject panics.
stop.writing_guide: Preserve the six-turn misunderstanding. Keep every turn extremely short and make the false definition drive the escalation.
anti_patterns: Do not use mental health, protected identity, or a real person's fear.
Do not squeeze explanatory prose into the six panels.

slots.role: First dialogue states the condition or role.
Second dialogue asks what it means.
Third dialogue gives the comic misunderstanding.
Fourth dialogue rejects that definition.
Fifth dialogue performs the misunderstood trigger.
Sixth dialogue tells Patrick to stop.

invariants: The wrong definition must directly motivate the fifth-line trigger and final reaction.
operator_example: Stop it, Patrick, you're scaring him

assessment.origin: A six-panel SpongeBob exchange about misunderstanding claustrophobia as fear of Santa Claus.
assessment.safety: The original hinges on fear and the six captions risk unreadable mobile text.
assessment.legibility: FAIL: six independent dialogue captions are too small to scan at the audited 360px width.
assessment.admission_rationale: Hold pending an exact phone-size render that proves six short lines remain readable without identity jokes.

vince.name: Vince McMahon Reaction
vince.meaning: Three options or revelations produce escalating excitement.
vince.writing_guide: Order three genuinely stronger benefits from good to extraordinary. Each line should be comparable on the same dimension.
anti_patterns: Do not use merely different options.
Do not use sexual or body-focused material from the original footage.

slots.role: First panel labels the good option.
Second panel labels the stronger option.
Third panel labels the strongest option.

invariants: Each successive item must intensify the same benefit or preference.

assessment.origin: Reaction sequence built from WWE footage of Vince McMahon showing escalating amazement.
assessment.safety: Real executive likeness. The source footage objectifies a performer, and current allegations create unrelated public-figure baggage.
assessment.legibility: PASS: every caption and image role remains readable in the exact 360px contact-sheet tile.
assessment.admission_rationale: Useful escalation structure, but hold because the recognizable subject now carries distracting safety baggage.

whatyear.name: What Year Is It?
whatyear.meaning: An outdated practice or uncanny recurrence makes the observer feel displaced in time.
whatyear.writing_guide: Name one concrete anachronistic practice on top and preserve the fixed question below.
anti_patterns: Do not use for a merely old technology still fit for purpose.
Do not stack a long list of nostalgic references.

slots.role: Top caption names the practice that feels out of time.
Bottom caption preserves the fixed disoriented question.

invariants: The first line must establish why the present situation feels like a different era.
operator_example: Copying orders from email into ERP

assessment.origin: Robin Williams's newly freed character in Jumanji asks the year after 26 years trapped in the game.
assessment.safety: Actor likeness. Keep the joke on outdated processes, not the actor or mental state.
assessment.legibility: PASS: every caption and image role remains readable in the exact 360px contact-sheet tile.
assessment.admission_rationale: Adds a concise anachronism reaction well suited to legacy workflows.

wkh.name: Who Killed Hannibal?
wkh.meaning: The actor who caused the failure immediately blames an unrelated party.
wkh.writing_guide: Label the harmed result, the responsible actor, and the false accusation.
anti_patterns: Do not depict or joke about violence.
Do not accuse a real organization without evidence.

slots.role: First label names what the actor damages.
Second label names the actor causing the damage.
Third caption blames someone else.

invariants: The second role must directly cause the first outcome and the final line must redirect blame.

assessment.origin: An Eric Andre Show sketch in which Andre shoots Hannibal Buress and asks who killed him.
assessment.safety: The visible shooting is inseparable from the established self-caused-blame joke.
assessment.legibility: PASS: every caption and image role remains readable in the exact 360px contact-sheet tile.
assessment.admission_rationale: Fails the campaign's violence and injury gate despite its useful blame-shifting relationship.
